page: Microsoft Azure M48ds_1_v3 belongs to the MDSMediumMemoryv3 instance family, hosted on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The virtual machine delivers 48 dedicated vCPUs built on Intel x86_64 architecture paired with 974.0 GB of RAM. This configuration provides a high memory allocation of approximately 20.29 GB per virtual processor, targeting environments that require extensive working memory.

Storage capabilities include 429 GB of bundled local SSD storage along with support for Premium Storage. The instance does not feature discrete GPU hardware, and complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included. From a qualitative perspective, the high RAM-to-CPU ratio allows workloads with substantial memory footprints to run without over-provisioning compute resources. However, the trade-off is a lower compute density relative to memory capacity, making it less cost-effective for pure compute-bound tasks.

Because of its significant memory volume and dedicated Intel compute allocation, the M48ds_1_v3 is suited for memory-intensive operations. Appropriate workloads include large in-memory databases, massive caching tiers, enterprise transactional systems, and heavy extract-transform-load (ETL) data pipelines requiring large in-memory datasets.
description: Microsoft Azure M48ds_1_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the MDSMediumMemoryv3 family running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by dedicated x86_64 Intel processors providing 48 vCPUs alongside an expansive 974.0 GB memory allocation, resulting in approximately 20.29 GB of RAM per core. For transient data handling and swap requirements, the system includes 429 GB of local SSD storage and supports Premium Storage configurations. It operates without discrete GPUs and does not bundle complimentary public IPv4 addresses. With a memory-to-core ratio exceeding twenty gigabytes per vCPU, this instance trades compute density for massive RAM capacity, making it qualitatively cost-effective for systems bottlenecked strictly by memory footprint rather than parallel CPU throughput. The hardware profile is tailored for large-scale in-memory databases, real-time caching systems, enterprise resource planning deployments, and intensive analytical processing.
